title: Reduce attribution overhang by streaming correction sidecar for console telemetry
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Background:
The Console telemetry pipeline occasionally produces 'attribution overhang' — late-arriving tokens and usage events that are not reconciled into the billing ledger within the expected settlement window. This leads to transient mismatches between console usage dashboards and the billing system, confusing SREs and customers during billing audits.

Problem statement:
- Late events (edge proxies, regional stalls, mobile clients) produce out-of-order ingestion that our batch reconciler only picks up hours later.
- Current reconciliation run is heavyweight and causes contention when reprocessing large deltas.
- Customers observe temporary under/over-charging in the console UI and file support tickets.

Goal:
Design and ship a small streaming "correction sidecar" that attaches to the ingestion tier to detect candidate overhangs, synthesize idempotent correction events, and route them through a lightweight streaming correction pipeline into the ledger writer. This should reduce visible console-vs-billing drift to < 1 hour for 95% of incidents and dramatically lower the size of batch replays.

Proposed approach:
1) Detection logic (ingestion sidecar): maintain per-tenant watermark heuristics using compact state (last-seen-event-time, seq gaps, max-latency). Flag candidate overhang windows when out-of-order arrival or sequence gaps exceed a threshold.
2) Correction event composer: create idempotent correction records that include provenance metadata (original event fingerprint, source, ingestion node id, causal timestamp). Corrections are tagged for a dedicated correction topic.
3) Streaming correction pipeline: lightweight Kafka/Stream job that validates corrections, enriches with customer plan / rate metadata, and forwards to a dedicated ledger-insert 'corrections' path that the ledger writer can process with non-destructive semantics.
4) Ledger writer change: support a corrections input that applies safe upsert semantics and emits audit markers that are surfaced to console dashboards and billing reconciler.
5) Observability & dashboards: new correction-rate and correction-latency SLOs, sample inspector for manually reviewing correction events, and an alert when correction rate spike indicates upstream regression.

Non-goals:
- This work does not replace the canonical batch reconciliation job; it reduces its load and latency.
- Not introducing new charging rules; corrections must preserve prior cost semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end closed-loop test demonstrates a late event arriving 45 minutes after original stream is visible in console totals within 15 minutes post-ingest for a tenant in staging.
- Correction records are idempotent: replaying same correction twice results in a single ledger effect (proof in integration test).
- Production telemetry shows reduction in average console-billing delta window from median ~3h to <= 45m within two weeks of rollout.
- New metrics emitted: correction_events_total, correction_latency_ms (p95/p99), correction_rejections_total.
- Rollout plan and runbook published and reviewed by SRE and Billing teams.

Technical risks and mitigations:
- False-positive corrections creating churn: add conservative thresholding and a dry-run flag for initial rollout to 10% of tenants.
- Ledger contention: corrections flow uses async upsert with limited concurrency and backpressure; add circuit breaker if backpressure > 80%.
- Schema drift for provenance fields: include versioned metadata block and migration fallback in ledger writer.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Week 0: feature flagged dry-run (no ledger writes) in us-east for internal tenants.
- Week 1: enable write path for low-volume tenants with manual reviewer on duty.
- Week 2: roll to 25% of production tenants with automatic sampling.
- Week 3: global rollout if SLOs met, decommission heavyweight batch replays that target the same windows.

Runbook highlights:
- If correction_rejections_total increases > 5x baseline: disable correction writer and switch to dry-run; open incident with data-team on call.
- If ledger write latency > 500ms for corrections: flip circuit breaker to queue corrections to cold path and page SRE.

Notes and trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep correction logic outside the main ingestion path to avoid adding tail-latency to every request. The sidecar runs co-located but processes asynchronously.
- Chose upsert semantics over compensation transactions to simplify downstream billing inference. This trades off richer audit trail vs operational simplicity.

2026-02-20 - Carlos Mendes: Prototype sidecar implemented; demoed dry-run correction payload format. Ran into a problem with tenant plan lookup latency — added local cache with TTL 30s.
2026-02-25 - Leah O'Connor (SRE): Reviewed rollout plan; added circuit breaker for corrections when ledger RT > 500ms. Suggested adding a sample inspector UI in Console.

2026-03-01 - Priya Singh (Billing): Confirmed corrections must preserve original per-token unit attribution; flagged billing report integration as dependency. We will not change rate logic in this ticket.
